calls.head: The Islanders can’t afford to take penalties
calls.body: The Devils’ power play is one of the league’s best, and the Islanders’ kill is one of the league’s worst. Every trip to the box hurts the Islanders more than most.
calls.call: The Devils’ power play creates at least their usual 8.5 expected goals per 60.
calls.nums: New Jersey 4th for power play (8.5 expected goals per 60) · NY Islanders 31st for penalty kill
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: New Jersey’s power play created 4.0 expected goals per 60 in 10:00 of 5-on-4 time, against their usual 8.5, and scored 0 goals.

calls.head: The Devils feed on mistakes, and the Islanders make them
calls.body: The Devils turn stolen pucks into chances, and the Islanders are one of the league’s worst at avoiding breakdowns. A sloppy pass or two could cost the Islanders.
calls.call: The Devils get at least their usual 7.6% of their 5-on-5 chances right after winning the puck.
calls.nums: New Jersey 6th for chances off turnovers (7.6% of their chances come right after winning the puck) · NY Islanders 31st for avoiding breakdowns
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: 11.9% of New Jersey’s 5-on-5 chances came right after winning the puck, against their usual 7.6%.

NYI.head: We gave NY Islanders a 33% chance, and NY Islanders proved us wrong.

NJD.head: We gave New Jersey a 67% chance, but NY Islanders had other ideas.

surprises.head: I. Sorokin stole one
surprises.body: I. Sorokin allowed 0 goals on shots worth 3.5 expected goals, 3.5 fewer than expected. Starting goalies had a night this good about once every 175 starts over the last three seasons.

surprises.head: NY Islanders brought the hits
surprises.body: NY Islanders’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 172, against their usual 94 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 50 games.

story.head: Sorokin shuts out the Devils
paras: Simon Holmstrom opened the scoring early in the second. Six different Islanders scored. Ilya Sorokin stopped all 37 shots.
The chances were closer than the score.

items.text: One of the preview’s two calls held.
